The ever improving Peter Eldridge was the outstanding performer of the day. In a full afternoon's running he successfully defended all three sprint titles.

Woodford Green's international David Jones running into the wind was first past the post in both sprints with 10.1 and 22.3. Peter Eldridge looked none to happy and was fifth in the longer race with 23.1. Neither of our two half-milers reached the 880yds final.
In a long-lasting battle for supremacy as Belgrave's best sprint man, Gerry LeRoy hoisted his penant high with a triple victory over close rival Peter Eldridge.

In a Bedfordshire v Hertfordshire match on May 21st Peter Eldridge won the 220 and 440 with 22.8 and 48.9, Norman Caves won the long jump and HSJ with 20"8' and 46'4', whilst Alan Spicer's 16.2 placed him 2nd in the 120yds hurdles-----A BELGRAVE field day!
After a bad start in the 200metres, in which he lay last at half-way, Peter Eldridge stormed thro' the field to take 2nd place in a fine 22.1secs.
At the same meeting Peter Eldridge and Ron Holtum gained their "London" vests; Peter doing 48.8 and Ron anchoring the relay team.

In the Great Britain v U.S.A. match on July 22nd, Peter Eldridge finished 4th in both the Invitation 100 yards (10.1) and 440 yards (48.7) events.

The highlight of this season, so far, is undoubtedly the struggle for supremacy between Peter Eldridge and Brian Morris, in the quarter-mile.
Peter Eldridge, running in the inside lane, had removed his stagger handicap before the runners had entered the third bend! He won by a good 15 yards in 49.0 seconds.

Bill Kerr, racing for the first time since his injury, ran a fine 14:14.6 three miles to finish 4th, but the remainder of our team, apart from Peter Eldridge, either failed to qualify for their finals or were outside the first six.
Peter Eldridge pulled off the treble once again. His times this year were, 100 yards - 9.9 seconds (equals Club record), 220 yards - 21.9 seconds, and 440 yards - 49.8 seconds.
Pride of place must surely be given to the four Belgrave boys, Peter Eldridge, Brian Morris, Graham Worrall, and Gerry Leroy, who gained second place in the A.A.A's 4 x 440 yds relay.

Peter Eldridge was of great value in the sprints and finished 3rd and 2nd in the 100 and 220 (10.4/22.7). Dave Cocks (50.0) and John Thresher (1:53.7) were both 3rd in the one and two lap events, with Geoff North following up with a 6th place in the (A) mile, 4:18.5.
The most pleasing thing about meeting was to see the welcome return of Peter Eldridge. He ran very well to finish 2nd in both sprints, and looks as if he will soon be back to his old form.

The Senior sprints were very disappointing, yet the nostalgic reminiscences that came to mind when we saw the return of those two great athletes Peter Eldridge and Gerry Leroy tended to make us overlook that there was only one other competitor in the 100 and 220.
